title: The page layout mode is specified with padding, and nothing implements it
foundBy: session agent, laying out the options for CUI-058 at the owner's request
details:
Section 2 of `DESIGN_SYSTEM_SPEC.md` lists three layout modes a feature may use inside the shell. The row for `page` reads "Centered max-width container with padding". Nothing in the package provides one. There is no component, no class and no token for a page container.

The sentence below that table hands the job to the consumer, and it covers width alone: "Each page's content area is responsible for applying its own width constraints". The padding the table promises is never assigned to anyone.

The preview shows what follows. Sixteen selectors in `preview/src/preview.css` set a `--space-4` padding on a pattern demo's root. Several demos carry it at two depths at once, `explorer-demo-11` alongside `explorer-demo-19`, and `master-detail-demo-17` alongside `master-detail-demo-190`. A comment in that file explains to the next reader that this padding is what makes the pages read as cards.

Three properties belong to a page container, and none of them has an owner. The inset from the window edge, the maximum width, and which element scrolls. The third is the expensive one: when no ancestor owns the scroll, content is clipped and unreachable, which is the failure the hidden Explorer tree recorded in CUI-011.

One more measurement bears on the fix. `scrollbar-gutter: stable` reserves the scrollbar's space so nothing shifts when it appears. It is used once in the repository, at line 62 of `src/styles/components/event-lanes.css`, and is named in no specification. A container that owns the scroll should carry it, and the design system should say so.
